raw_segments.text: Then we will once more entreat Homer, and the other poets not to depict Achilles, who
is the son of a goddess, first lying on his side, then on his back, and then on his face,
then starting up and sailing in a frenzy along the shores of the barren sea, now taking the
sooty ashes in both his hands and pouring them over his head, or weeping and wailing
in the various modes which Homer has delineated.
Nor should he describe Priam the kinsman of the gods as praying and beseeching.
